source_title: National Payment Systems Directives on Electronic Money Issuance, 2023
publisher: Bank of Zambia; published in the Republic of Zambia Government Gazette as Gazette Notice No. 958 of 2023
intended_use: Potential consumer-protection clauses on failed local transactions and complaint-information duties; keep review-only until currentness is confirmed.
verification_notes: Official BoZ-hosted directive explicitly replaces the 2018 directive and contains customer-protection provisions 32(2)(a)–(c), 32(2)(f), and 32(4). Gazette pagination shows July 2023; printed headers include both 14 and 24 July, so publication date is stored at month precision only. Follow-up checked the official directives listing and the 2024 National Payment Systems Annual Report. The 2024 report describes a separate directive on unwarranted charges for electronic money services; it does not establish whether the 2023 provisions remain in force, were amended, or were replaced. Current legal status remains unconfirmed; KB027–KB028 remain review-only.

Printed p.3 says BoZ issued the 2024 Prohibition against Unwarranted Charges and Fees on Electronic Money Services Directives during 2024 to protect consumer rights. It reports mobile-payment usage, campaigns and issuance of unwarranted-charge directives but provides no current customer how-to guide.
